experiment_b_drift_analysis.divergence_definition: Pairwise layer-wise L2 norm: sum_l ||W_{alpha, l} - W_{beta, l}||_2
experiment_b_drift_analysis.forensic_explanation: In Experiment B, Client Divergence is defined as the pairwise layer-wise L2 norm between Hospital Alpha and Hospital Beta weights post-local training: sum_l ||W_{alpha, l} - W_{beta, l}||_2. The increase in client divergence from 0.97 (1-step smoke test) to 10.3 (full 236-step round) is consistent with executing significantly more local optimization steps on heterogeneous client data cohorts. However, parameter divergence in non-convex neural network optimization is not expected to scale linearly with step count due to diminishing gradient magnitudes, weight decay regularization, optimizer momentum decay, and the geometry/curvature of the loss surface constraining local trajectory drift.

quantity_distinction.explanation: The global parameter delta norm (||W_global^{r} - W_global^{r-1}||_2 ≈ 4.49) measures the net shift of the aggregated centroid. The actual quantity in the FedProx proximal penalty is the local client displacement (||w_client - w_global||_2 ≈ 6.0 - 8.5). With ||w_client - w_global||_2^2 ≈ 36 - 72, mu = 0.01 produces a proximal penalty of (0.01/2)*50 ≈ 0.25, representing ~25-35% of the base DiceCELoss (~0.65-0.95).

fedprox_configuration_design.scientific_rationale: With mean local client parameter displacement ||w_client - w_global|| ≈ 6.0-8.5, mu = 0.01 yields a proximal penalty of ~0.18-0.36, which represents ~20-35% of the base DiceCELoss value (~0.65-0.95). This provides a calibrated proximal regularization force that constrains client drift without freezing local adaptation.

1_step_empirical_metrics.note: At step 1 forward pass, local weights equal global weights before gradient step, yielding exact 0 proximal penalty.
